history.summary: CSV town 'Kota' is CORRECT - the documented referent is the Karneshwar Mahadev Temple on Karneshwar Road, Kota Bypass (Barda Basti / Talab Gaon, Anantpura, Kota 324010), a Shiva temple that doubles as one of Kota's favourite monsoon picnic spots: rainwater cascades down the rocky slope above the temple, creating natural pools where visitors bathe, and vendors sell pakodis and corn - reviewers call it a 'free natural water park'. AMBIGUITY FLAG: sources conflate this temple with the ancient Kansua/Kansuwa Shiva temple (famous four-faced shivling; site where James Tod found a 5th-century inscription in 1820) - one travel page explicitly calls 'Karneshwar temple' another name of Kansua Temple, and the geocoder resolves 'Karneshwar Mahadev Temple' to 'Karneshwar Mahadev Temple-Kansuwa'. The Kota Bypass/monsson-picnic identity (Instagram, Yappe, Justdial, Wanderlog listings at 25.101021, 75.854207) is the best-supported referent for this CSV row; whether the Bypass temple and the Kansua temple are the same shrine or two distinct ones could not be resolved from available sources - verify on the ground. HOURS CONFLICT: Justdial/Yappe/Instagram list 6:00 AM-6:00 PM daily; placeapp.in and velpu.com list 6:00 AM-9:00 PM - verify before visiting.

name: Karneshwar Mahadev Temple
town: Kota (Kota Bypass, Karneshwar Road, Barda Basti/Anantpura - CSV town 'Kota' is correct)
town_description: Kota is Rajasthan's coaching capital on the Chambal river. The Karneshwar Mahadev Temple sits on Karneshwar Road off the Kota Bypass, in the Talab Gaon/Anantpura area on the city's outskirts (about 2.6 km from Dadhdevi railway station). The rocky, scrub-covered terrain around it turns lush in the monsoon, when the temple's waterfall setting makes it a popular family picnic and bathing spot.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport (Sanganer) - about 245 km; Kota airport has limited connectivity (verify).
travel.railway: Dadhdevi station - about 2.6 km (per Yappe); Kota Junction - major junction on the Delhi-Mumbai line.
travel.road: On Karneshwar Road, Kota Bypass - about 10-20 minutes from the main city by auto-rickshaw, taxi or private vehicle (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: Monsoon (July-September) for the waterfalls and greenery - this is the peak picnic season; winter (October-March) for comfortable sightseeing. Mondays are the busiest day.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 6:00 AM-6:00 PM daily by Justdial/Yappe/Instagram, and as 6:00 AM-9:00 PM by placeapp.in/velpu - CONFLICT, verify on site.
